56.description: Saskatoon will develop a policy to manage city land for affordable housing, potentially involving buying land at market and selling below market, which could impact city finances.

chips.text: Approved
11 for, 0 against
Councillor Goodwill clarified that the city would pay for infrastructure on development-ready sites.
Councillor Donauer requested an estimate of potential money loss if land is sold below market.
Staff committed to providing an overview of all city funding for housing and homelessness.

57.description: Saskatoon will issue a Request for Proposals to lease and manage the public market at River Landing, with the 120 Sonnenschein Way commercial space as an optional component.

chips.text: Approved
11 for, 0 against
Entrepreneurs and business owners at Gather and Ideas Inc. are directly affected.
A tenant advocated for including both market spaces in the RFP to maintain community.

66.description: The proposed plan for dedicated bus lanes on 1st Avenue, which would have removed 61 parking stalls and impacted traffic flow, was defeated.

chips.text: Defeated (5-6)
5 for, 6 against
Downtown Saskatoon has abundant parking capacity, and the project improves access for everyone.
Ready Properties, owning 77,000 square feet downtown, expressed concerns about the plan.
Administration requires Council direction to report specific plans to advisory committees.
The geometric feasibility of a shorter dedicated lane section on 1st Avenue remained unaddressed.
Downtown business groups raised concerns about parking loss and difficulties with delivery access.
Councillor Davies questioned dedicated lanes on a specific two-block section of 1st Avenue.
A transit policing program will be fully staffed by 2027 to support BRT safety.

67.description: Saskatoon exempted Fire Stations 10 and 11 from the Net Zero Energy Ready target due to design challenges and budget, though they will still be the city's most energy-efficient fire halls.

chips.text: Approved
11 for, 0 against
Staff could not provide energy cost projections beyond one year.
Fire Station 11 is the first new civic facility designed under the 2021 policy.
Staff will bring an interim report on policy adjustments in the next few months.

81.description: Saskatoon will fund $275,900 for year-round homelessness services, including outdoor washrooms and women's drop-ins, and investigate options for future winter and annualized funding.

chips.text: Approved
10 for, 0 against
Councillor Dubois questioned why the city is not actively seeking private donations for services.
Saskatoon Tribal Council operates the drop-in services and provides peacekeepers.
Winter 2026/2027 men's overnight and daytime drop-in locations are still unknown.
Services include a women's overnight drop-in at 325 Avenue C South.
Administration will report back on 2026/2027 winter plans and annualized funding options.

79.description: Council approved bylaws for the 2026 Saskatoon property tax, school division property tax, and Business Improvement District levy, enabling tax billing to begin in May.

chips.text: Approved
10 for, 0 against
Property owners and businesses in Business Improvement Districts are affected.

80.description: Saskatoon approved a new collective agreement with The Society of United Professionals, including 2.5-3% annual raises, DEI initiatives, and paid cultural days for employees.

chips.text: Approved
10 for, 0 against
Affects employees of The Society of United Professionals, IFPTE Local No. 160.
Includes a pilot program to enhance representation of designated groups.
City committed to supporting mental health and well-being initiatives.

chips.text: First reading passed (10-0)
